E13-C1.claim: persistence is as good as the age-structured model for 8-yr population
E13-C1.evidence: model pop MAPE 0.09% vs hold-2015-flat 3.45% - age structure earns its place

E13-C2.claim: Keyfitz momentum is not a stable regional constant (it depends on base year)

E13-C3.claim: USA 'population predictability' is migration persistence, not age-structure momentum
E13-C3.evidence: 2016-23 cumulative natural 5915k vs migration 10940k - migration dominates the USA change

E13-C4.claim: the USA shortfall is not pure recoverable tempo - its quantum (adjTFR) is itself falling since 2010
E13-C4.evidence: USA adjTFR slope 2010-23 = -0.050/yr - quantum declining, not just postponement (tempo estimates noisy)

E13-C5.claim: the tempo/quantum split is fragile - r=d(MAC)/dt is noisy and flips sign repeatedly
E13-C5.evidence: USA r sign-flips 0 over 34 yrs, std 0.045 - the mean age rises monotonically, split is stable

E13-C6.claim: Korea's deficit is partly tempo too - its mean age at childbearing is still rising
E13-C6.evidence: Korea recent r = +0.194/yr - postponement ongoing, so not a pure quantum deficit

E13-C7.claim: Rogers-Castro is unnecessary for the population TOTAL - a scalar (age-uniform) migration matches it
E13-C7.evidence: USA total residual: RC 0.228% vs age-uniform 6.451% - the age shape matters even for the headline total

E13-C8.claim: migration, not fertility, is the USA master variable to 2100 (+50% migration beats +0.3 TFR)
E13-C8.evidence: USA 2100: +0.3 TFR +85.9M vs +50% migration +61.7M - fertility is the stronger lever

E13-C9.claim: the Rogers-Castro childhood-echo term is redundant - a labour-peak-only schedule matches the total
E13-C9.evidence: USA total residual: RC-full 0.228% vs labour-only 0.889% - the echo earns its place

E13-C10.claim: a modest (+0.3) fertility lift is futile for Korea - it recovers a tiny fraction of the baseline loss
E13-C10.evidence: Korea +0.3 TFR recovers 18% of the 32M baseline loss - modest but non-trivial

E13-C11.claim: for the USA a migration lever dominates any fertility intervention to 2100
E13-C11.evidence: USA 2100 levers: migration +61.7M vs fertility +85.9M - fertility is competitive, not dominated

E13-C12.claim: intervention timing barely matters at the 2100 horizon (2025 vs 2045 start)
E13-C12.evidence: Korea early-vs-late structural lift differ 34% of 2100 pop - timing is decisive, not minor

E13-C13.claim: 'momentum locks the near term' is arithmetic, not insight - 2050's mothers are already born
E13-C13.evidence: 97% of Korea's 2050 births come from women already alive in 2023 - the near-term lock is arithmetic

E13-C14.claim: the 'TFR-1.5 trap ridge' is behavioural lore, not the Leslie replacement threshold (~2.1)
E13-C14.evidence: USA TFR at NRR=1 (lambda=1) = 2.09 - the 1.5 ridge is an empirical trap, NOT a mathematical replacement boundary

E13-C15.claim: the Leslie eigenvalue does not order strictly by TFR (survival reshuffles near-ties)
E13-C15.evidence: lambda-order ['France', 'USA', 'Germany', 'Spain'] vs TFR-order ['France', 'USA', 'Germany', 'Spain'] - orders coincide, lambda tracks TFR

E13-C16.claim: migration wrecks the stable-pyramid match - the eigenvector is a poor fit to the actual pyramid
E13-C16.evidence: USA cos(stable eigenvector, actual 2023 pyramid) = 0.976 - still strong despite migration

E13-C17.claim: the low in-sample MAPE is over-flexibility - the model fits pure white noise just as well
E13-C17.evidence: w2 fit to random-noise TFR gets MAPE 11.28% - it does NOT fit noise well; in-sample fit is meaningful

E13-C18.claim: the closed gap is an in-sample illusion - true one-step-ahead (train<=2022) misses 2023
E13-C18.evidence: USA train<=2022 -> 2023 gap 0.103 (in-sample was 0.009) - one-step-ahead is still hard (an honest limit)

E13-C19.claim: MI-usage near 1 is memorization not information - a saturated interpolator scores MI=1 by construction
E13-C19.evidence: a per-year interpolation (median=data) scores MI-usage 1.00 - MI alone cannot separate signal from memorization

E13-C20.claim: the frozen-rate baseline is a strawman - a random-walk-with-drift baseline beats it
E13-C20.evidence: held-out TFR MAPE: frozen 8.77% vs RW-drift 6.17% - the model should beat the stronger baseline, not the frozen one

E13-C21.claim: the '0.00% deaths fidelity' is unimpressive - crude-rate x population reproduces deaths anyway
E13-C21.evidence: crude CDRxPop deaths MAPE 0.47% - the death TOTAL needs no age structure (the pyramid matters for its age profile)

E13-C22.claim: the full age model doesn't reorder regions - 2023 TFR rank already predicts the 2100 outcome rank
E13-C22.evidence: Spearman(TFR-2023, 2100 %change) = 0.71 across 7 regions - TFR ranks, but migration/structure reorder (rho<0.8)

E13-C23.claim: 'demographic collapse' overstates it - no study population approaches extinction this century
E13-C23.evidence: worst 2100 ratio (Korea) 0.37 of 2023 - a halving-and-ageing, not an absorbing extinction; 'collapse' is a decline, not a vanishing

E13-C24.claim: sub-replacement is not destiny within the model - steady migration stabilizes Korea despite TFR 0.72
E13-C24.evidence: Korea needs 459k/yr net migration (0.89% of pop/yr) to hold flat to 2100 - demographically plausible

E13-C25.claim: the 'momentum governs' finding has low falsifiability - the calibration has more knobs than data points-per-region
E13-C25.evidence: per-region latent DOF ~37 vs 34 data points - the defensible, parameter-free evidence is operator fidelity + held-out backtest, not the fit
